Misc. Appeal No. 880 of 2
 Vardichand And Others

 Sampat And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Pourush Ranka, learned counsel for the appella  Shri Abhay Chand Jain, learned counsel for responde  Insurance Company.
RESERVED ON   PRONOUNCED ON :

O The present Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 20.01.2015 passed in Claim Case No.53/2013 challenging the quantum of compensation.
02. Facts of the case in short are that on 28.02.2012, son of the present appellant namely Vikram and his friend were going towards their village through motorcycle.

At around 04:45 pm, near Kachnara Suvasara Road at Jhalaara Fantaa, respondent No.1 came driving pick up vehicle bearing registration No.RJ 06 GA 5105 in rash and negligent manner and collided with the motorcycle.
Because of accident, Vikram died on the spot NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:260 2 MA-880-2015 due to the grievous injuries sustained by him.

Dashrath also suffered grievous injuries and he remained unconscious for three days and was hospitalized for about 21 days.
03.
The appellants / claimant filed a claim petition under Section 163(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act claiming compensation on account of death of their son in the accident.
The Claims Tribunal, after assessing the evidence that came on record, has awarded an amount of Rs.3,44,000/-.
Being aggrieved, the present miscellaneous appeal is before this Court.

04. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned Tribunal has committed legal and factual error in holding the monthly income of deceased as Rs.3,000/-, whereas he was having annual income of Rs.40,000/-.

The Tribunal has erred in making a deduction for the personal expenses of 1/2 from the total income to deceased which is not permissible as the claim has been Vardichand vs Sampat on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166295063/
1 filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicle Act.

entities.text: Vardichand vs Sampat on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation of Rs.3,44,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side and the same is liable to be enhanced.
05. Learned counsel appearing for Insurance Company supports the findings of the Claims Tribunal and submits that it is a clear case of contributory negligence.
Hence, this appeal be dismissed.
06. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
07. In the present case, the original application was filed under Section 163(A) of the Motor Vehicle Act.

As per para - 1 of the impugned award, the same was passed under Section 163(A), therefore,
there is no need NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:260 3 MA-880-2015 to deal with this M.A. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act.

08. As per para - 33 of the impugned award, the age of the deceased was assessed to be between 15 - 20 years, therefore, as per Second Schedule of Section 163-A (the then provision), multiplier of 16 was applicable.
The learned counsel for the Insurance Company has agreed to deceased's income (estimated) to be Rs.40,000/- per year.

09. In light of the judgement of the Apex Court in the case Kurvan Ansari alias Kurvan Ali & Another v/s Shyam Kishore Murmu & Another reported in (2022) 1 SCC 317 , Rs.40,000/- each (total Rs.80,000/-) is liable to be awarded towards loss of consortium.
10.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari alias Kurvan Ali & Another v/s Shyam Kishore Murmu & Another reported in (2022) 1 SCC 317
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the judgment of Pranay Sethi v/s National Insurance Company reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 , 40% future prospect income is liable to be awarded.

entities.text: Pranay Sethi v/s National Insurance Company reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. Hence, the impugned awarded passed by the learned Claims Tribunal is hereby modified to the extent indicated as under:-
HEAD AMOUNT OF COMPENSATION Rs.4,345/- + 1,738/- (Future prospects 40%) Income Taken Rs.6,083/- (per month) x 12 =72,996/- x 16 - 1/3 = 7,78,624/-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000/- each (Total Rs.8  Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
. The learned Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,44,000/-.

Thus, the appellants are held entitled to receive enhanced amount of Rs.5,44,624/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal, making total compensation amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:260 4 MA-880-2015 Rs.8,88,624/-.
12.
With the aforesaid, Miscellaneous Appeal stands allowed in part.
(ALOK AWASTHI) JUDGE Ravi Vardichand vs Sampat on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166295063/
